text:
alex: Hey team — customer in APAC needs exact egress allowlist and port guidance for calling our hosted inference API. They want to lock down outbound firewall rules + proxy. Any gotchas?
mira: Short answer: allow our region CIDRs + 443, allow DNS, and let ephemeral TCP ports through for NAT. But details below.
julian: +1. We publish per-region CIDR blocks but explain why IPs can shift. For customers that require stable IPs, recommend Dedicated or Private with static NAT.
alex: Where can I point them for the CIDR list? They asked for concrete example rules to hand to their security team.
mira: Send them our published list (doc link) and include these examples (use as minimal set):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 203.0.113.0/24 (apac), 198.51.100.0/24 (us-east fallback)
- Allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to customer's DNS resolver (we need DNS resolution)
- Allow ephemeral outbound ports 1024-65535 (for NAT source ports)
- Health checks from load balancers may come from other ranges — recommend permitting inbound responses (established) only.
julian: Important: do NOT rely on IP-based allowlist for long term; TLS SNI filtering can be brittle because of SNI removal or SNI routing. Best practice: allow egress by FQDN (api.redwood.ai) via proxy that supports HTTPS CONNECT.
samir: If they have a proxy, they must allow CONNECT to port 443 (proxy port 8080/3128) and permit TLS passthrough. Example curl test to verify from their proxy: 
```
curl -x http://proxy.company.local:3128 -I https://api.redwood.ai/health
```
ops-bot: Deploy-bot: canary rollout to apac finished — egress IP pool refreshed at 2026-02-18T09:12Z (info only).
alex: Any DNS TTL concerns? They will whitelist hostnames and rely on DNS TTL caching.
mira: TTLs can be short (60s-300s) for some internal endpoints. If they use FQDN allowlist on their firewall, ensure it re-resolves frequently or is handled by a proxy that resolves per-connection.
julian: Also warn them about NAT IP rotation during scaling or failover. If they pin a single IP and we failover, connections might break. Suggest allowing the whole CIDR block we publish rather than single IPs.
samir: Note on ports: besides 443/80, we use occasional GRPC endpoints over 443 only. No extra inbound ports required. If they have deep packet inspection that intercepts TLS, service identity might fail. Recommend exception for our domain.
mira: If they run an outbound proxy with TLS interception, they must add our cert public key to the allowlist or disable interception for api.redwood.ai — otherwise request signing and cert pinning may fail.
alex: Anything about ephemeral port exhaustion / NAT resources? Security team worried about many connections during batch inference spikes.
julian: Yes — advise them to increase NAT pool size and ephemeral port range. Recommend monitoring SNAT exhaustion. If they see port exhaustion, suggest enabling reuse or scaling NAT gateways.
samir: Example firewall rule snippet (for their ops ticket):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood (APAC)
allow tcp dst 203.0.113.0/24 dst-port 443
allow udp dst-port 53 # for DNS
allow tcp dst-port 53 # DNS over TCP fallback
allow tcp dst-ports 1024-65535 established
```
mira: Last note: if they need absolute IP stability we can offer a static egress IP add-on on Dedicated/Private. Otherwise, FQDN via proxy + CIDR allowlist is the least painful route.
alex: Perfect — I'll paste this into the security ticket and link the published CIDRs. Thanks everyone :+1:
